rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two-woman provision explains the testimony rule: if one forgets, the other reminds her; al-Alusi attributes forgetfulness to women’s temperaments.
rows.anchor: شرع ذلك إرادة أن تذكر إحداهما الأخرى إن ضلت إحداهما لما أن النسيان غالب على طبع النساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An objection says God’s legal will should not target forgetfulness; al-Alusi answers that the will targets the reminder consequent on it, not the lapse itself.
rows.anchor: لم تتعلق بالضلال نفسه أعنى عدم الإهتداء للشهادة بل بالضلال المرتب عليه الإذكار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction with an means reminder is so strongly desired that the normally unwanted lapse appears to be sought as its means; this is better than calling lapse a metonym for reminder.
rows.anchor: الإيماء إلى شدة الإهتمام بشأن الإذكار بحيث صار ما هو مكروه كأنه مطلوب لأجله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second one of them can be the subject of remind, or its object while the other is subject; neither parse forces a misplaced explicit noun.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن تكون فاعل تذكر وليس من وضع المظهر موضع المضمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Putting the explicit object before the subject foregrounds reminding the woman who forgot; repeating the noun also avoids assigning forgetfulness to one particular woman.
rows.anchor: والسبب في تقديم المفعول على الفاعل التنبيه على الإهتمام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Masud’s reading, transmitted by al-Aʿmash, has her remind her; other grammarians say the canonical wording intensifies ambiguity about which woman forgets.
rows.anchor: وهي قراءة ابن مسعود كما رواه الأعمشى إلى ما في النظم الكريم لتأكيد الإبهام

rows.speaker: حسين بن علي المغربي
rows.claim: Al-Maghribi takes the first one of them as one of the two testimonies and the second as one of the two women, so one woman recalls the forgotten testimony.
rows.anchor: فجعل ضمير ( إحدهما ) الأولى راجعا إلى الشهادتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi rejects al-Maghribi’s testimony-as-subject reading: it breaks the syntax and leaves no sensible second one; al-Tabarsi’s lexical support is weak because Arabic calls a forgetful person ضال.
rows.anchor: وليس بشئ إذ لا يكون لإحداهما أخرى في الكلام مع حصول التفكيك وعدم الإنتظام

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير والضحاك والربيع والسدي
rows.claim: These early authorities are reported as using ضل for a person who forgets, supporting the ordinary reading of the verse.
rows.anchor: وقد روي ذلك في الآية عن سعيد بن جبير والضحاك والربيع والسدي

rows.speaker: ابن عيينة
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUyayna is reported to interpret the two women together as equivalent to a male witness; al-Alusi rejects this as strained in meaning and syntax.
rows.anchor: ما حكي عن ابن عيينة أن معنى ( فتذكر ) الخ فتجعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi says making two women into one figurative male witness requires layered metaphors and still fails to explain the need for a male witness if both women are present.
rows.anchor: لأن الإحتياج إلى اقتران ذكر البتة معهما

rows.speaker: شهاب الدين الغزنوي
rows.claim: In the Khafaji anecdote, the judge answers that repeating one of them preserves ambiguity; a pronoun would wrongly identify a particular woman as the one subject to the ruling.
rows.anchor: تضل إحداهما ) فالقول محتمل كليهما فهي للاظهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A passive feminine reading of an tadilla is reported, along with the variant فتذاكر.
rows.anchor: وقرئ ( أن تضل ) بالبناء للمفعول والتأنيث وقرئ فتذاكر

rows.speaker: ابن كثير ويعقوب وأبو عمرو والحسن
rows.claim: These readers recite فتذكر with a still dhal and kasra on kaf.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير ويعقوب وأبو عمرو والحسن فتذكر بسكون الذال وكسر الكاف

rows.speaker: حمزة
rows.claim: Hamza reads an tadilla as a conditional clause and فتذكر in the indicative; its syntax is discussed in the next segment.
rows.anchor: وحمزة ( أن تضل ) على الشرط فتذكر بالرفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammarians variously supply an omitted subject after the conditional fa; one analysis supplies the remembered woman, while other accounts supply a story pronoun or a pronoun for testimony.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الأوجه أن يقدر المبتدأ ضمير الذاكرة

rows.speaker: بعض المحققين
rows.claim: Some exacting grammarians prefer an implicit dual pronoun after the fa: then the two women remind one another.
rows.anchor: الأوجه من هذا كله تقدير ضمير التثنية أي فهما تذكر إحداهما الأخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi says later grammarians misunderstood al-Zamakhshari’s analogy to 5:95: the point is an omitted pronoun supplied by context, not whether it is singular or dual.
rows.anchor: ولم يتفطنوا بأن ذلك إنما هو من جهة تقدير ضمير بعد الفاء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas and al-Hasan are cited for interpreting the witnesses’ refusal as refusal either to give testimony or to undertake it.
rows.anchor: وهو المروي عن ابن عباس والحسن رضي الله تعالى عنهم

rows.speaker: مجاهد وابن جبير
rows.claim: Mujahid and Ibn Jubayr restrict the prohibition to refusing to give testimony.
rows.anchor: وخص ذلك مجاهد وابن جبير بالأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi finds refusal to give testimony the more apparent sense because it avoids figurative interpretation, though al-Rabiʿ’s reported occasion points to being asked to testify.
rows.anchor: وهو الظاهر لعدم إحتياجه إلى إرتكاب المجاز

rows.speaker: الربيع
rows.claim: Al-Rabiʿ says the verse came when a man went around asking many people to witness and nobody responded.
rows.anchor: أن الآية نزلت حين كان الرجل يطوف في القوم الكثير فيدعوهم إلى الشهادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle ma after idha is an extra particle, a regular construction.
rows.anchor: صلة وهى قاعدة مطردة بعد ( إذا )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saʾama means to tire of or become annoyed by something; the verse discourages weariness over recording debt.
rows.anchor: ولا تسئموا ( أي تملوا أو تضجروا

rows.speaker: زهير
rows.claim: Zuhayr’s line supplies poetic evidence for the sense of saʾima, growing weary.
rows.anchor:
ومنه قول زهير :
سئمت تكاليف الحياة ومن يعش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of writing may be the debt, right, or written record implied by the verb; the verb can take it directly, or an understood preposition may be omitted.
rows.anchor: أي الدين أو الحق أو الكتاب المشعر به الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some take saʾama as laziness by euphemism, since the Qurʾan describes hypocrites as praying lazily; a hadith says a believer should say prayer feels burdensome, not lazy.
rows.anchor: وقيل : المراد من السأم الكسل إلا أنه كني به عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reads both occurrences of yasʾamu in the plural masculine form.
rows.anchor: وقرئ ولا يسأموا أن يكتبوه بالياء فيهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Small and large describe the debt’s amount or its level of detail; alternatively they are predicates of an omitted kāna, with the smaller stated first for emphasis and progression.
rows.anchor: حالان من الضمير أي على كل حال قليلا أو كثيرا مجملا أو مفصلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase to its term describes the debt remaining due until its agreed maturity, not the writing, which takes little time.
rows.anchor: حال من الهاء في تكتبوه أي مستقرا في ذمة المدين إلى وقت حلوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That may refer to writing, testimony, or, best, all the preceding practices; the demonstrative addresses the believers.
rows.anchor: أي الكتب وهو الأقرب أو الأشهاد وهو الأبعد أو جميع ما ذكر وهو الأحسن

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh allows the comparatives aqsaṭ and aqwam to be formed directly from verbs, without treating them as irregular.
rows.anchor: مبينان من أقسط وأقام على رأى سيبويه

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan, citing Ibn al-Qattaʿ, says qasṭ means justice, so aqsaṭ needs no special derivation from a noun.
rows.anchor: وقيل من قاسط بمعنى ذى قسط وقويم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aqwam retains its wāw because the root is frozen in the exclamatory form; the comparative has a meaning that supports this form.
rows.anchor: وإنما صحت الواو فى أقوم ولم يقل أقام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Writing and witnessing make doubts about a debt’s kind, amount, and maturity less likely; the omitted preposition before an taرتابوا is variously understood as ila, lam, min, or fi.
rows.anchor: أقرب إلى انتقاء ريبكم وشككم في جنس الدين وقدره وأجله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cash-trade exception is best read as a detached exception from the writing command: immediate exchange of both countervalues permits leaving the transaction unwritten.
rows.anchor: استثناء منقطع من الأمر بالكتابة

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: The Dur al-Masun allows a connected exception from witnessing: cash trade is exempt from witnessing in every case.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون استثناءا متصلا من الاستشهاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other analyses make the exception detached from both writing and witnessing, or attach it to both; al-Alusi favors the first analysis.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إنه استثناء من هذا وذاك وهو منقطع أيضا

rows.speaker: عاصم
rows.claim: Asim reads tijaratan in the accusative as the predicate of kāna, with an implicit subject referring to trade.
rows.anchor: ونصب عاصم تجارة على أنها خبر تكون واسمها مستتر فيها يعود إلى التجارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other grammarians make the implied subject refer to the transaction and treat trade as a verbal noun; most readers use the nominative, with trade as subject and the clause as predicate, or take kāna as complete.
rows.anchor: ورفعها الباقون على أنها اسم ( تكون ) ولخبر جملة ( تديرونها )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no harm or sin in omitting written records for immediate exchanges, because they are less exposed to dispute and forgetfulness or because writing them is burdensome.
rows.anchor: أي فلا مضرة عليكم أو لا إثم في عدم كتابتكم لها لبعد ذلك عن التنازع والنسيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Witness when you make the specified sale, or, according to a broader reading, whenever a sale is made.
rows.anchor: أي هذا التبايع المذكور أو مطلقا

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: Umar’s uncontracted reading with kasra supports the active interpretation of the prohibition against harming a scribe or witness.
rows.anchor: قراءة عمر رضي الله تعالى عنه ولا يضار بالفك والكسر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas’s uncontracted reading with fatha supports the passive interpretation, forbidding others to harm the scribe or witness.
rows.anchor: وقراءة ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما بالفك والفتح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If active, the verse forbids witnesses and scribes to refuse, distort, add, or subtract; if passive, it forbids burdening them, withholding the fee, or requiring costly travel.
rows.anchor: نهى الكاتب والشاهد عن ترك الإجابة إلى ما يطلب منهما وعن التحريف والزيادة والنقصان

rows.speaker: الربيع
rows.claim: Al-Rabiʿ reports that requesters sometimes forced busy scribes to write and would not let them decline; this occasion explains the command not to harm them.
rows.anchor: ما أخرجه ابن جريح عن الربيع قال : لما نزلت هذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi rejects making the صيغة carry both active and passive meanings at once.
rows.anchor: وحمل بعضهم الصيغة على المعنيين وليس بشئ

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan is reported to read the verb with kasra; a nominative variant treats the negative as a prohibition.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ولا يضار بالكسر وقرئ بالرفع على أنه نفي بمعنى النهى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warned-against act is the prohibited harm or another breach; فسوق بكم means disobedience attached to you, or more forcefully a state in which you are immersed.
rows.anchor: منكم ( فإنه ( أى ذلك الفعل ( فسوق بكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows every matter and will repay people for their conduct.
rows.anchor: فلا يخفى عليه حاكم وهو مجازيكم بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating the divine name in three successive independent clauses is laudable when it magnifies the subject; here the clauses exhort piety, promise divine instruction, and glorify God’s knowledge.
rows.anchor: المستحسن كل تكرير يقع على طريق التعظيم أو التحقير في جمل متواليات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clauses differ as exhortation, promise, and declaration, which explains their connective pattern; treating the middle clause as a circumstantial clause is possible but less preferred.
rows.anchor: لأن ( اتقوا الله ) حث على تقوى الله تعالى ( ويعلمكم الله ) وعد بإنعامه سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being upon a journey is a dependent metaphor for being firmly established in travel; the clause may coordinate with the conditional verb or describe a state.
rows.anchor: ففيه استعارة تبعية حيث شبه تمكنهم في السفر بتمكن الراكب من مركوبه

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: Abu al-Aliya reads kutuban, while al-Hasan and Ibn Abbas read kitaban.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو العالية كتبا والحسن وابن عباس كتابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rahn can mean the means of security, something to be taken, or the prescribed pledge; rahn began as a verbal noun and then named the pledged object.
rows.anchor: وهو في الأصل مصدر ثم أطلق على المرهون من باب إطلاق المصدر على اسم المفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The travel and lack of a scribe indicate when a pledge substitutes for documentary security, not conditions on its validity; the Prophet pledged his armor to a Jew in Medina for thirty measures of barley.
rows.anchor: بل لإقامة التوثق بالارتهان مقام التوثق بالكتبة في السفر

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid takes the verse literally and permits pledges only during travel.
rows.anchor: وأخذ مجاهد بظاهر الآية فذهب إلى أن الرهن لا يجوز إلا في السفر

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says a pledge during travel is lawful only when no scribe is available.
rows.anchor: وكذا الضحاك فذهب إلى أنه لا يجوز في السفر إلا عند فقد الكاتب

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority require the pledge to be physically delivered to complete it.
rows.anchor: والجمهور على وجوب القبض في تمام الرهن

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik holds that offer and acceptance complete the pledge and make delivery binding; if the pledge returns absolutely to the debtor’s hand, it leaves the pledge and shares among creditors.
rows.anchor: وذهب مالك إلى أنه يتم بالإيجاب والقبول ويلزم الرهن بالعقد تسليمه

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu Ali’s verse uses rahin for bread and meat as things still held or remaining, illustrating the pledge’s implication of continuity.
rows.anchor: أنشد أبو على : فالخبز وللحم لهن راهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive adjective maqbudah suggests that a proxy’s possession suffices; the mortgagee need not personally take possession.
rows.anchor: وفي التعبير بمقبوضة دون تقبضونها إياءا إلى الاكتفاء بقبض الوكيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other readings have rahun, with a rounded plural pattern, or rahn with a light, vowelless ha.
rows.anchor: وقرئ فرهن كسقف وهو جمع رهن أيضا وقرئ بسكون الهاء تخفيفا

rows.speaker: أبي
rows.claim: Ubayy’s reading makes the debtor’s trustworthiness passive: people have entrusted him and described him as faithful and reliable.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبي فإن أو من أي أمنه الناس ووصفوا المديون بالأمانة والوفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If some trust others, the debt is left unsecured by writing, witnesses, or pledge, whether they are traveling or resident.
rows.anchor: بعض الدائنين بعض المديونين بحسن ظنه سفرا أو حضرا فلم يتوثق بالكتابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person entrusted is the debtor, named by that description to identify him and encourage repayment; amānah denotes the debt owed.
rows.anchor: وهو المديون وعبر عنه بذلك العنوان لتعينه طريقا للإعلام ولحمله على الأداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The debt is called a trust because the creditor has left it unsecured, relying on the debtor to repay; the possessive pronoun can refer to creditor or debtor.
rows.anchor: وإنما سمى أمانة وهو مضمون لائمانه عليه بترك الإرتهان به

rows.speaker: عاصم
rows.claim: Asim’s assimilated reading of the hamza-derived form is criticized by some as an error, but al-Alusi cites its attestation in Arabic and the Kufan grammatical position permitting it.
rows.anchor: وعن عاصم أنه قرأ الذتمن بإدغام الياء في التاء وقيل هو خطأ

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Al-Saghani cites Aisha’s fluent speech as an Arabic parallel for assimilation, recorded in al-Bukhari as the Prophet directing her to wear a waist wrapper.
rows.anchor: وورد مثله فى كلام أم المؤمنين عائشة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to fear God at repayment, as at the original acknowledgment, stresses human rights and guards against betrayal and corruption.
rows.anchor: وقد أمر سبحانه بالتقوى عند الوفاء حسبما أمر بها عند الإقرار تعظيما لحقوق العباد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not conceal testimony by refusing to give it when summoned; the address is to believing witnesses, as transmitted from early authorities.
rows.anchor: أي لا تخفوها بالامتناع عن أدائها إذا دعيتم إليها

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr and others are cited for reading the command as addressed to witnesses.
rows.anchor: وهو خطاب للشهود المؤمنين كما روي عن سعيد بن جبير وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative address to debtors, meaning they should acknowledge debt or avoid defeating witnesses in court, conflicts with the apparent wording and early transmitted interpretation.
rows.anchor: خلاف الظاهر المأثور عن السلف الصالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reads the verb for concealing in the third-person plural.
rows.anchor: وقرئ يكتموا على الغيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in innahu most naturally returns to whoever conceals testimony; some make it a pronoun of the matter, though a following participial phrase is not a sentence for Basran and Kufan grammarians.
rows.anchor: الضمير فى أنه راجع إلى ( من ) وهو الظاهر وقيل : إنه ضمير الشأن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammarians parse āthim as predicate with qalb as its subject, as predicate before a delayed subject, or with qalb in apposition; al-Farra and al-Akhfash also allow qalb as the subject of āthim, a construction most grammarians reject.
rows.anchor: وهذا جائز عند الفراء من الكوفيين والأخفش من البصريين وجمهور النحاة لا يجوز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attributing the sin to the heart is concise because concealment is an inward act; naming the chief organ intensifies the warning and shows the enormity of the sin.
rows.anchor: ولأن الإثم وإن كان منسوبا إلى جملة الشخص لكنه اعتبر الإسناد إلى هذا الجزء المخصوص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi dismisses additional explanations that the attribution alludes to a black mark from sin or to the heart’s effect on the whole body.
rows.anchor: والكل ليس بشئ كما لا يخفى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant puts qalb in the accusative by analogy with an object; Abu Hayyan permits it as partitive apposition, while some call it specification and Abu al-Baqa rejects that.
rows.anchor: وقرئ قلبه بالنصب على التشبيه بالمفعول

rows.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
rows.claim: Ibn Abi ʿAbla reads āthama qalbahu, making the heart sinful.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبى عبلة ( آثم قلبه ) أى جعله آثما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows whether people conceal testimony or deliver it properly and will repay them accordingly.
rows.anchor: والله بما تعملون من كتمان الشهادة وأدائها على وجهها وغير ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God repays each person according to the conduct at issue: good is repaid with good and evil with evil.
rows.anchor: فيجازيكم بذلك إن خيرا فخير وإن شرا فشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah closes by urging believers to hold fast to its guidance and meet enemy stratagems, after recounting rulings, believers’ and unbelievers’ states, and believers’ suffering.
rows.anchor: ختم السورة بما يضوع منه مسك التمسك بما مضى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sabr means restraining oneself from distress; the apparent command includes the three forms of patience named in a report: through affliction, obedience, and refraining from sin.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن المراد الأمر بما يعم أقسام الصبر الثلاثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sābirū means outlasting the enemy in the hardships of war; it follows general patience because it is harder and thus more excellent.
rows.anchor: أي أصبروا على شدائد الحرب مع أعداء الله تعالى صبرا أكثر من صبرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The coordination of sābirū after ṣbirū resembles singling Gabriel out after mentioning the angels, or the middle prayer after prayers generally.
rows.anchor: فالعطف كعطف جبريل على الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rābiṭū means to remain at frontier posts, horses held and ready for a raid, surpassing the enemy in readiness; this too is a kind of patience.
rows.anchor: أقيموا في الثغور رابطين خيولكم فيها حابسين لها مترصدين للغزو

rows.speaker: سهل بن سعد
rows.claim: Sahl ibn Saʿd reports from the Prophet that a day of frontier duty is better than the world and everything in it.
rows.anchor: أخرج الشيخان عن سهل بن سعد أن رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم قال

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A sound report in Ibn Majah says one who dies guarding the frontier continues to receive his righteous deeds and provision and is kept safe from the interrogators and the great terror.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن ماجه بسند صحيح عن أبي هريرة رضي الله تعالى عنه عن رسول الله

rows.speaker: جابر
rows.claim: Jabir reports in a chain al-Tabarani calls acceptable that one day of frontier duty places seven trenches between a person and the Fire, each as wide as seven heavens and earths.
rows.anchor: أخرج الطبراني بسند لا بأس به عن جابر قال : سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Abu al-Shaykh transmits from Anas, with the Prophet as authority, that prayer in frontier territory is worth two million prayers.
rows.anchor: وأخرج أبو الشيخ عن أنس مرفوعا الصلاة بأرض الرباط بألف ألفي صلاة

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar says frontier duty is superior to jihad because it protects Muslim lives, while jihad spills the blood of polytheists.
rows.anchor: وروى عن ابن عمر رضي الله تعالى عنهما أن الرباط أفضل من الجهاد لأنه حقن دماء المسلمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taqwa here means obeying God’s commands generally, encompassing all the preceding commands.
rows.anchor: وأتقوا الله في مخالفة أمره على الإطلاق فيندرج فيه جميع ما مر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Falah means winning one’s aim, attaining the desired goal, and succeeding in one’s pursuit.
rows.anchor: أي لكي تظفروا وتفوزوا بنيل المنية ودرك البغية والوصول إلى النجح

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One elaborate interpretation divides human life into individual and communal duties: patience covers religious reasoning, worship, avoidance of sins, and worldly hardship, while steadfastness covers social forbearance, counsel, and jihad.
rows.anchor: أحوال الإنسان قسمان الأول ما يتعلق به وحده والثاني ما يتعلق به من حيث المشاركة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: That interpretation makes ribat discipline the soul’s powers, taqwa guard all action from vanity and ostentation, and falah the divine reward after worship’s duties are complete.
rows.anchor: أمره سبحانه بالمرابطة أعم من أن تكون مرابطة ثغر أو نفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi calls the elaborate scheme strained and prefers that the commands form a straightforward progression.
rows.anchor: ولا يخفى أنه على ما فيه تمحل ظاهر وتعسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: General patience comes first because it is like the head to the body and the key to relief.
rows.anchor: إنه تعالى أمر بالصبر العام أولا لأنه كما في الخبر بمنزلة الرأس

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: A maxim says reason is the human being’s jewel and patience the intellect’s jewel; religious and worldly attainments come only through patience, as the cited poet says.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : لكل شيء جوهر وجوهر الإنسان العقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second command advances from general patience to jihad, a special patience that brings public benefit and honor; a prophetic warning links abandoning jihad with divinely imposed humiliation until return to religion.
rows.anchor: وقد جاء عن رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم إذا تركتم الجهاد سلط الله تعالى عليكم ذلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ribat is a still higher form of patience: holding a frontier against an anticipated threat.
rows.anchor: ثم ترقى إلى نوع آخر من ذلك هو أعلى وأغلى وهو المرابطة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: General taqwa concludes the sequence because ostentation, self-admiration, and attention to other than God could corrupt the preceding acts.
rows.anchor: لولاها لأوشك أن يخالط تلك الأشياء شيء من الرياء والعجب

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra tells Salama ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman that the verse addressed people who maintained mosques, prayed at the appointed times, and remembered God there; patience means the five prayers, steadfastness resisting the self, and ribat remaining in mosques.
rows.anchor: أقبل على أبو هريرة يوما فقال

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A report shared by Malik, al-Shafiʿi, Ahmad, and Muslim says thorough ablution despite hardship, frequent steps to mosques, and waiting from one prayer to another erase sins and raise ranks; that waiting is called ribat three times.
rows.anchor: وأخرج مالك والشافعي وأحمد ومسلم عن أبي هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi says the mosque report may be sounder than the earlier report, but its claim that no frontier fighting existed in the Prophet’s time is far-fetched and hardly defensible.
rows.anchor: ولعل هذه الرواية عن أبي هريرة أصح من الرواية الأولى مع ما في الحكم فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if sound, the mosque report does not contradict the standard interpretation: the definite ribat can mean frontier duty, while the Prophet compares mosque observance to it as a figure of speech.
rows.anchor: لا تنافي التفسير المشهور لجواز أن تكون اللام في الرباط فيها للعهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the allusive reading, the heavens and earth signify upper and lower worlds, night and day darkness and light, and people of understanding see creation through the Real.
rows.anchor: أي العالم العلوي والعالم السفلي ( وإختلاف الليل والنهار ) الظلمة والنور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembering God while standing signifies witnessing in the spirit, sitting signifies unveiling in the heart, and lying on one’s sides signifies striving amid the soul’s transformations.
rows.anchor: في مقام الروح بالمشاهدة ( وقعودا ) في محل القلب بالمكاشفة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another allusive reading takes standing as obedience to commands, sitting as avoidance of prohibitions, and reclining as avoiding attention to acts of disobedience.
rows.anchor: أي قائمين بإتباع أوامره ( وقعودا ) أي قاعدين عن زواجره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Contemplation means either the heart’s immersion in hidden stores of the lights of divine attributes to know power, or the heart’s movement through creation to behold its Creator.
rows.anchor: وذلك التفكر على معنيين الأول طلب غيبة القلوب في الغيوب التي هي كنوز أنوار الصفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation is not vain: it mirrors God’s names and manifests His attributes; Labid’s verse says all things other than God are transient.
rows.anchor: بل هو مرايا لإسمائك ومظاهر لصفاتك ويفصح بالمقصود قول لبيد

rows.speaker: لبيد
rows.claim: Labid’s poem witnesses the transience of everything beyond God and every pleasure.
rows.anchor: ألا كل شيء ما خلا الله باطل وكل نعيم لا محالة زائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In this reading, glorifying God denies any existence besides Him, and the Fire is the veil of created things that blocks vision of the Creator.
rows.anchor: أي تنزيها لك من أن يكون في الوجود سواك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Entering the Fire means being veiled from vision and abased by distance from God; the wrongdoers are those who assign existence to what has none.
rows.anchor: وتحجبه عن الرؤية ( فقد أخزيته ) وأذللته بالبعد عنك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wrongdoers have no helpers because the overpowering manifestation dominates them.
rows.anchor: من أنصار ) لإستيلاء التجلي القهري عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The caller to faith is the innermost secret by the spirit’s valley, calling to direct, witnessed faith; believing means beholding God.
rows.anchor: من أسرارنا التي هي شاطيء وادي الروح الأيمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the caller is God’s primordial address to spirits in the covenant of alast; their assent was the reply bala after witnessing Him.
rows.anchor: والمراد به هو الله تعالى حين خاطب الأرواح في عالم الذر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The supplication asks that traits of the self be covered by divine attributes, bad acts by witnessing divine acts, and the self be ended through chosen death, joining those established in unity.
rows.anchor: ذنوب صفاتنا بصفاتك ( وكفر عنا ) سيئات أفعالنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised good is the best and an increase; not being disgraced means not being veiled by divine favor, and God never breaks His promise.
rows.anchor: ( للذين أحسنوا الحسنى وزيادة ) ( ولا تخزنا يوم القيامة )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The male is the heart with its works of sincerity and certainty; the female is the soul when it abandons spiritual struggle and bodily worship; both share the human spirit’s single origin.
rows.anchor: القلب وعمله مثل الإخلاص واليقين ( أو أنثى ) النفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Migration is turning from everything but God toward God, expulsion from homes is leaving the self’s habits, and persecution by deniers is necessary for the sweetness of closeness, as Junayd says.
rows.anchor: من غير الله تعالى إلى الله عزوجل ( وأخرجوا من ديارهم )

rows.speaker: الجنيد
rows.claim: Junayd thanks his brothers because their harsh treatment returned him to God; they fought the self and killed it with the sword of annihilation.
rows.anchor: جزى الله تعالى إخواننا عنا خيرا ردونا بجفائهم إلى الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forgiveness removes small and great remnants of selfhood; the three gardens signify acts, attributes, and essence, their rivers knowledge and theophanies, and all reward belongs to God.
rows.anchor: الصغائر والكبائر من بقايا صفاتهم وذواتهم ( ولأدخلنهم جنات ) ثلاث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unbelievers’ movement through lands means those veiled from unity moving through worldly states and spiritual stations; its benefit is brief and quickly vanishes.
rows.anchor: أي حجبوا عن التوحيد ( في البلاد ) في المقامات الدنيوية والأحوال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell is deprivation from God, a wretched resting place chosen according to the unbelievers’ preparedness.
rows.anchor: الحرمان ( وبئس المهاد ) الذي أختاروه بحسب أستعدادهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pious attain three gardens instead, prepared by God; what is with Him means the blessings of vision, nearness, and union.
rows.anchor: ثلاث عوض ذلك ( نزلا من عند الله ) معدا لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers among the People of the Book realize unity and knowledge of the origin, return, and spiritual ranks; they humble themselves before divine manifestation, and their reward is the gardens.
rows.anchor: ويحقق التوحيد الذاتي ( وماأنزل إليكم ) من علم التوحيد والإستقامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s signs are manifestations of His attributes; the reward arrives without delay because His accounting is swift.
rows.anchor: تعالى وهي تجليات صفاته ( ثمنا قليلا أولئك لهم أجرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One allusive reading means patience against sins, steadfastness in obedience, spiritual binding through direct witnessing, and guarding against seeing anything besides God; success is release from worries and thoughts.
rows.anchor: عن المعاصي ( وصابروا ) على الطاعات ( ورابطوا ) الأرواح بالمشاهدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, patience belongs to the soul’s struggle, steadfastness to the heart amid manifestations, and ribat to the spirit holding the self against weakness or heedlessness.
rows.anchor: أصبروا ) في مقام النفس بالمجاهدة ( وابروا ) في مقام القلب مع التجليات

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Ibn al-Sunni, Abu Nuʿaym, and Ibn ʿAsakir transmit from Abu Hurayra that the Prophet recited these final ten verses of Ali ʿImran.
rows.anchor: أخرج ذلك ابن السني وأبو نعيم وابن عساكر عن أبي هريرة

rows.speaker: عثمان
rows.claim: The Darimi transmits from Uthman that whoever recites the end of Ali ʿImran at night is granted the reward of a night’s vigil.
rows.anchor: وأخرج الدارمي عن عثمان قال : من قرأ آخر آل عمران

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Tabarani transmits a prophetic report from Ibn Abbas that whoever recites the surah containing Ali ʿImran on Friday receives God’s and the angels’ blessings until sunset.
rows.anchor: وأخرج الطبراني من حديث إبن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما مرفوعا من قرأ السورة التي يذكر فيها آل عمران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi labels fabricated the report promising safety on the bridge over Hell for every verse of Ali ʿImran and censures exegetes who transmitted it.
rows.anchor: أعطى بكل آية أمانا على جسر جهنمموضوع مختلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi closes his commentary on al-Fatiha and the two Zahrawayn, hoping God will enable him to complete the tafsir through the two refuge-seeking surahs.
rows.anchor: و ليكن هذا خاتمة ما أمليته من تفسير الفاتحة والزهراوين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nisa is Medinan according to the correct view; al-Nahhas calls it Meccan based on the Meccan revelation of the command to return the Kaaba key, but al-Suyuti says that does not determine the whole surah’s provenance.
rows.anchor: ( مدنية على الصحيح وزعم النحاس أنها مكية مستندا إلى أن قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: السيوطي
rows.claim: Al-Suyuti argues that a Meccan verse within a long surah, mostly revealed in Medina, does not make that surah Meccan; material after the Hijra is generally Medinan.
rows.anchor: لأنه لا يلزم من نزول آية أو آيات بمكة من سورة طويلة نزل معظمها بالمدينة

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha’s report in al-Bukhari that Baqara and Nisa were revealed while she was with the Prophet, after their post-Hijra marriage, supports Nisa’s Medinan classification.
rows.anchor: ما أخرجه البخاري عن عائشة رضي الله تعالى عنها قالت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says the surah was revealed around the time of the Hijra.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إنها نزلت عند الهجرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Syrian count is 177 verses, the Kufan count 176, and other counts 175; authorities differ on whether two clauses are separate verses.
rows.anchor: وعدة آياتها عند الشاميين مائة وسبع وسبعون وعند الكوفيين ست وسبعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nisa opens with taqwa after Ali ʿImran ends with it, a strong rhetorical link between surahs known as similarity of endings or tassbigh.
rows.anchor: آل عمران ختمت بالأمر بالتقوى وأفتتحت هذه السورة به وذلك من آكد وجوه المناسبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other links are that Nisa refers to the aftermath of Uhud, follows Ali ʿImran’s mention of the expedition after Uhud, and develops in detail themes stated earlier; this ordering is better than that in Ibn Masud’s codex.
rows.anchor: في آل عمران ذكر قصة أحد مستوفاة وفي هذه السورة ذكر ذيلها

rows.speaker: شيخ الإسلام
rows.claim: Shaykh al-Islam says the command begins specifying when and on what condition orphan wealth is returned, following the general order to give it and the ban on entrusting it to fools.
rows.anchor: شروع في تعيين وقت تسليم أموال اليتامى إليهم وبيان شرطه بعد الأمر بإيتائها على الإطلاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This connection is clearer if the earlier fools are wasteful orphans; it is less clear if all orphans are called foolish based on their childhood, as another account has it.
rows.anchor: على تقدير أن يراد من السفهاء المبذرين بالفعل من اليتامى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view treats the verse as a return to orphan-property rulings rather than a new beginning, on the premise that the preceding material was a digression.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إن هذا رجوع إلى بيان الأحكام المتعلقة بأموال اليتامى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guardians are addressed; test orphans by observing their ability to manage property and transact prudently.
rows.anchor: والخطاب للأولياء والإبتلاء الإختبار أيوأختبروا

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa takes sound financial management as the test’s criterion.
rows.anchor: والإقتصار على هذا الإهتداء رأي أب يحنيفة

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafiʿi additionally requires uprightness in religion, a view also attributed to Ibn Jubayr, Ibn Abbas, and al-Hasan.
rows.anchor: والشافعي رحمه الله تعالى يعتبر مع هذا أيضا الصلاح في الدين

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة والشافعي
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa and al-Shafiʿi agree that the trial takes place before puberty, as the verse’s endpoint indicates; Malik places it after puberty.
rows.anchor: وأتفق الإمامان رضي الله تعالى عنهما على أن هذا الإختبار قبل البلوغ

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa reasons that testing before puberty requires permission for a discerning minor to buy and sell under the guardian’s supervision.
rows.anchor: لأن ذلك الإختبار إنما يحصل إذا أذن له في البيع والشراء مثلا

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafiʿi says testing need not authorize transactions or hand over property: the guardian can make the contract after observing the minor’s ability.
rows.anchor: الإختبار لا يقتضي الإذن في التصرف لأنه يتوقف على دفع المال إلى اليتيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reaching marriageable age means puberty, through a wet dream or age; fifteen is the limit for al-Shafiʿi, Abu Yusuf, Muhammad, and a transmitted Hanafi position adopted in the school.
rows.anchor: أي إذا بلغوا حد البلوغ وهو إما بالإحتلام أو بالسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common arrival at marriageable fitness by fifteen supports that age; al-Bayhaqi himself calls weak the report from Anas that property records and legal penalties begin at fifteen.
rows.anchor: لما أن العادة الفاشية أن الغلام والجارية يصلحان للنكاح وثمرته في هذه المدة

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: The well-known Hanafi view sets puberty at eighteen for boys and seventeen for girls, based on reaching maturity; Ibn Abbas and al-Qutaybi are cited for eighteen.
rows.anchor: وشاع عن الإمام الأعظم أن السن للغلام تمام ثماني عشرة سنة وولجارية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One report from Abu Hanifa gives nineteen for a boy, meaning he enters his nineteenth year after completing eighteen; the transmissions vary.
rows.anchor: وعنه في الغلام تسع عشرة سنة والمراد أن يطعن في التاسعة عشرة

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafiʿi is often said to use pubic hair growth as evidence of puberty among captured polytheists whose true age is unknown, deciding whether to apply adult or child treatment.
rows.anchor: وشاع عن الإمام الشافعي أنه قد جعل الإنبات دليلا على البلوغ في المشركين خاصة

rows.speaker: ابن حزم
rows.claim: Ibn Hazm denounces al-Shafiʿi over the pubic-hair ruling; al-Alusi says the denunciation is unwarranted because it is only a practical marker in a case where age cannot be known.
rows.anchor: وشنع ابن حزم الضال عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The captured adolescent might lie to avoid death, unlike a Muslim; examination therefore supplies an indicator in this case, not a separate general puberty criterion for unbelievers.
rows.anchor: ولا يخفى أن هذا لا يصلح محلا للتشنيع

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid explains anastum as perceived or sensed.
rows.anchor: فإن أنستم ( أي أحسستمقاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anasa originally described looking toward an approaching person with a hand shielding the eye, then broadened to perception; the verse may use literal or figurative perception.
rows.anchor: وأصل معنى الإستئناسكما قال الشهاب التظر من بعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poet’s use of anastu for perceiving a sound as evening approaches supports the verb’s sense of noticing.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر : ( آنست ) نبأة وأفزعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some derive anasa from the eye’s pupil and take its original meaning to be seeing generally; al-Alusi leaves both literal and figurative senses possible here.
rows.anchor: وزعم بعضهم أن أصله الإبصار مطلقا وأنه أخذ من إنسان العين

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud’s variant ahastum drops one doubled s after shifting its vowel; it may instead be a regular Sulaymi dialect pattern for doubled roots with attached pronouns.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود أحستم بحاء مفتوحة وسين ساكنة وأصله أحسستم

rows.speaker: أبو زيد الطائي
rows.claim: Abu Zayd al-Taʾi’s verse supplies evidence for the dialectal treatment of a doubled verb with a pronoun.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إنها لغة سليم وإنها مطردة في عين كل فعل مضاعف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rushd means financial discernment and prudent management, or, in another view, religious rectitude as well as sound financial judgment.
rows.anchor: أي إهتداءا إلى ضبط الأموال وحسن التصرف فيها وقيل : صلاحا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readers pronounce rushd with either fatha or damma, both meaning maturity; another distinction assigns worldly and afterlife maturity to the damma and only afterlife maturity to the fatha.
rows.anchor: وقريء رشدا بفتحتين ورشدا بضمتين وهما بمعنى رشدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fa in give them their property signals prompt delivery at the point of entitlement; some also see a semantic distinction between paying it over here and the earlier verb give.
rows.anchor: من غير تأخير عن حد البلوغ كما تدل عليه الفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hatta can introduce a full clause without losing its endpoint sense; here the conditional clause sets the end of testing and its fulfillment governs delivery.
rows.anchor: وتسمى ابتدائية في ذلك ولا يذهب منها معنى الغاية

rows.speaker: ابن مالك
rows.claim: Ibn Malik treats a later condition as modifying the first like a circumstantial clause; a competing analysis makes the first condition’s answer serve as the answer to subsequent ones.
rows.anchor: وزعم ابن مالك أن الشرط الثاني مقيد للأول بمنزلة الحال

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: The preferred grammatical analysis makes each later condition’s answer implicit from the preceding answer, requiring the conditions to occur in reverse nesting order; al-Jassas says Muhammad and Abu Yusuf also dispute the issue.
rows.anchor: والصحيح في هذه المسألة أن الجواب للأول وجواب الثاني محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other jurists make the final condition and its answer govern the preceding ones; some require all conditions in any order, while conjunctions alter which conditions the answer covers.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض الفقهاء : الجواب للأخير والشرط الأخير وجوابه جواب الثاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi endorses the lower-complexity analysis associated with al-Zamakhshari and al-Zajjaj: hatta governs the whole temporal clause, idha remains temporal, and delivery follows puberty plus financial maturity.
rows.anchor: وما نحن فيه من المقرون بالفاء وهي رابطة للجواب كالفاء الثانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contrast between idha for puberty and in for maturity reflects certainty of the former and uncertainty of the latter.
rows.anchor: وعبر في البلوغ بإذا وفي الإيناس بإن للفرق بينهما ظهورا وخفاءا

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says property is not returned even if an orphan’s hair turns gray unless financial maturity is perceived.
rows.anchor: به قال مجاهد فقد أخرج إبن المنذر وغيره عنه أنه قال : لا يدفع إلى اليتيم ماله

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafiʿi and the two Hanafi disciples follow the verse’s apparent requirement that property is withheld if puberty arrives without financial maturity.
rows.anchor: وهو مذهب الشافعي وقول الإمامين وبه قال مجاهد

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa requires delivery seven years after puberty even without perceived maturity, because the period permits change and education; he reads the earlier general command to give orphans their property as applying after puberty.
rows.anchor: إذا زادت عل ى سن البلوغ سبع سنين وهي مدة معتبرة فى تغير الأحوال

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: Umar is cited as saying a man’s intellect reaches completion at twenty-five.
rows.anchor: فقد ورد عن عمر رضي الله تعالى عنه أنه قال : ينتهي لب الرجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi reasons that time and experience eventually remove childhood traces and produce some maturity because this is the mind’s age of completion.
rows.anchor: وإذا أمتد الزمان وظهرت الخبرة والتجربة لم يبق أثر الصبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The philosophers’ biological argument doubles the earliest period in which a boy could father a child and that child could in turn reproduce.
rows.anchor: ففي هذه المدة يمكن أن يولد له ابن ثم ضعف هذا المبلغ يولد لابنه ابن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi notes that the Hanafi argument from give the orphans their property depends on reading it as delivery after puberty, an interpretation already debated.
rows.anchor: على أن المراد بالإيتاء فيها الدفع وقد مر الكلام في ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Critics argue that if any maturity inevitably appears by twenty-five, Abu Hanifa’s position collapses into the other imams’ rule; al-Alusi says financial competence need not arise by that age, while generic maturity would not satisfy the verse.
rows.anchor: إذا كان ضرب من الرشد كافيا كما يشعر به التنكير وكان ذلك حاصلا لا محالة في ذلك السن

rows.speaker: الفخر
rows.claim: Al-Fakhr says the test concerns protecting property, so the required maturity is competence in managing its interests; otherwise the verse’s clauses would be disconnected.
rows.anchor: لا شك أن المراد من ابتلاء اليتامى المأمور به ابتلاؤهم فيما يتعلق بمصالح حفظ المال

rows.speaker: الفخر
rows.claim: Al-Fakhr’s clear analogy says an adult or elder without the reason needed to preserve and use property should remain barred from it just as a child is.
rows.anchor: فإذا كان هذا المعنى حاصلا في الشاب والشيخ كانا في حكم الصبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi condemns Ibn Hazm and his Shiʿi followers for vilifying Abu Hanifa over this subsidiary disagreement while often relying on weaker evidence elsewhere.
rows.anchor: ولقوة كلام المخالف في هذه المسألة شنع الضال ابن حزم كعادته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi defends Abu Hanifa: once an orphan reaches adulthood, he is accountable for belief, worship, choice, reward, and punishment, so keeping his property under another’s control resembles oppression.
rows.anchor: كان منع ماله عنه وتصرف الغير به أشبه الأشياء بالظلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although this reasoning might warrant immediate payment at puberty even without competence, payment is delayed until twenty-five to allow education, maturity, and restraint from waste.
rows.anchor: إلا أنا أخرنا الدفع إلى هذه المدة للتأديب ورجاء الرشد والكف عن السفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The delay resembles, in one respect, holding the property of rebels until they return to obedience.
rows.anchor: ونظير ذلك من وجه أخذ أموال البغاة وحبسها عنهم ليفيئوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seven years was chosen because it commonly changes a child’s capacities; ten also marks change in the prayer hadith, but the lower sufficient period is adopted.
rows.anchor: واعتبرت الزيادة سبع سنين لأنهاكما تقدممدة معتبرة في تغير الأحوال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi denies that the restriction turns on every kind of foolishness or remains in force indefinitely; the relevant condition is childish incapacity and the legal school does not infer absence of consequence automatically from absence of a condition.
rows.anchor: بل مع سفه الصبا ولا نسلم بقاءه بعد تلك المدة على أن التعليق بالشرط لا يوجب العدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning against consuming orphan property wastefully and before they grow supports Abu Hanifa’s view that property should not be withheld once they have grown, with the special delay for an immature adult explained earlier.
rows.anchor: فإنه مشير إلى أنه لا يمنع مال اليتيم عنه إذا كبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Israf is exceeding what is permitted, by excess or shortfall; asrafa usually names excess and sarafa deficiency, while heedlessness or error is not intended here.
rows.anchor: والإسراف في الأصل تجاوز الحد المباح إلى مالم يبح وربما كانذلك في الإفراط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mubadara means haste: the guardian may rush to consume the property before the orphan grows, while the orphan may hasten to reclaim it; the word is linked to fullness.
rows.anchor: والمبادرة المسارعة وهي لأصل الفعل هنا وتصح المفاعلة فيه بأن يبادر الولي أخذ مال اليتيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The etymological examples are the full moon, a money bag filled with money, and a grain heap filled with food.
rows.anchor: ومنه البدر لامتلائه نورا والبدرة لامتلائها بالمال والبيدر لامتلائه بالطعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two coordinated accusatives are parsed as circumstantial accusatives, though some parse them as purpose clauses; this warning connects with the preceding prohibition, not the post-puberty conditional.
rows.anchor: والأسمان المتعاطفان منصوبان على الحال كما أشرنا إليه وقيل : إنهما مفعول لهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With fatha, kabura concerns age; with damma it denotes capacity or eminence, and with ala it describes something burdensome.
rows.anchor: بفتح الباء الموحدة من باب علم يستعمل في السن وأما بالضم فهو في القدرة والشرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition singles out eating, the basic and common use of wealth, so other forms of consuming it are prohibited all the more.
rows.anchor: وتخصيص الأكل الذي هو أساس الانتفاع وتكثر الحاجة إليه بالنهي يدل على النهي عن غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This warning reinforces the order to hand over the property and prepares for the rule distinguishing a wealthy guardian from a poor one.
rows.anchor: وفي الجملة تأكيد للأمر بالدفع وتقرير لها وتمهيد لما بعدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A wealthy guardian or trustee must refrain from using the orphan’s property and live on the wealth God gave him.
rows.anchor: ومن كان من الأولياء والأوصياء ذا مال فليكف نفسه عن أكل مال اليتيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istiafaf means to restrain oneself and is stronger than afaf; taking it as dignified avoidance explains the practical sense.
rows.anchor: فالإستعفاف الكف وهو أبلغ من العف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poor guardian may eat from the property only according to recognized custom and to the necessary amount for food and clothing, as ʿAtaʾ and Qatada say.
rows.anchor: بقدر حاجته الضرورية من سد الجوعة وستر العورة قاله عطاء وقتادة
